events.title: Iran to Declare New Restricted Zone Near Hormuz as Tanker Traffic Hits 4-Month Low; CENTCOM Says 92 Vessels Redirected, Oil Extends Gains
events.detail: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said on state television September 6 that Tehran will declare a new restricted maritime zone within days, running from the line of the US naval blockade outward through the Strait of Hormuz and into portions of the Persian Gulf; any vessel identified as intending to transit the Strait while inside the zone would be added to Iran's sanctions list, with consequences for insurance coverage and future access to the waterway. Rezaei separately said maps for a new international shipping corridor through Iranian and Omani waters had been agreed and were expected to be signed in the coming days. The announcement came as commercial tanker traffic through the Strait fell to its lowest level since May — an average of just 10 vessels a day over the prior 10 days versus 15+ on the preceding Friday, and only two vessels on Saturday, per shipping-analytics firm Kpler cited by Reuters. US Central Command said it has redirected 92 commercial vessels, disabled three, and boarded two since ramping up enforcement of the blockade, and released footage of an F-35A stealth fighter patrolling the waterway. Oil extended its rise into the new week: Brent crude rose toward $97.39/bbl (WTI ~$92.32), building on the prior week's roughly 8% gain, even as US equity markets were closed for Labor Day; European shares were mixed, with the Stoxx 600 little changed after falling 0.81% the week before.

events.title: August Jobs Report Blowout — Payrolls Surge 162,000 vs 53,000 Expected, Stocks Slip as September Hike Odds Jump to 60%
events.detail: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' August 2026 Employment Situation report, released Friday, showed nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 — dramatically ahead of the roughly 53,000-65,000 consensus forecast among economists polled by Dow Jones — while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%. The prior two months were revised up: June's gain was revised from +20,000 to +31,000 (+11,000) and July's from -23,000 to +21,000 (+44,000), lifting combined June-July employment by 55,000 versus previously reported. By industry, food services and drinking places added 59,000 jobs and local government education added 42,000, while information employment fell 23,000 on continued weakness in computing infrastructure, data processing/web hosting, publishing, and broadcasting. The report reversed a one-day-old dovish narrative: coming just a day after Fed Governor Waller signaled openness to a September hold, the blowout payrolls number sent CME FedWatch odds of a September 16 rate hike jumping to roughly 60.4% (from about 49.4% the day before), since strong employment gives the Fed more room to keep tightening against above-target inflation. Stocks fell on the news despite — or because of — the strength: the S&P 500 slipped about 0.3-0.5%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped roughly 245-300 points (about 0.5-0.7%) to around 53,325, and the Nasdaq Composite eased about 0.2-0.4%; the 10-year Treasury yield held around 4.76%. Semiconductor names outperformed on the day (Nvidia +1.4%, AMD +4.2%, SanDisk +10.4%, Micron +4.6%), while Lululemon sank as much as 17.4% after missing revenue targets, unrelated to the jobs data. Analysts said the report 'does lean toward the Fed increasing rates' on September 16, though cautioned it was 'not a foregone conclusion' given two more inflation prints due before the meeting.

events.title: US Dollar Falls as Fed and Treasury Bond Rescue Efforts Raise Stability Concerns
events.detail: The US dollar declined as investors weighed the Federal Reserve and Treasury's bond rescue efforts, signaling renewed concerns about dollar stability. The intervention measures, designed to support the bond market, instead prompted questions about underlying demand for US debt and the longer-term trajectory of the currency.

events.title: Treasury Yield Relief From Bessent's Buyback Doubling Reverses Within a Day
events.detail: One day after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Wednesday that Treasury would at least double the size of its long-end buyback operations — from $2 billion to $4 billion per operation across the 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year sectors, effective September 9 through November 4 — the relief rally reversed. Wednesday's announcement had pulled the 10-year note down 5.7 basis points to 4.647% and the 30-year bond down 9 basis points to 5.196%, with Bessent signaling the buyback size could go even higher. But by Thursday, yields on the 10-year moved back up more than 5 basis points to 4.704% and the 30-year rose a similar amount to 5.248%, erasing the prior day's gains as traders concluded the buyback program does not address the underlying structural drivers of the bond selloff — a near-record fiscal deficit and national debt nearing $40 trillion.

events.title: Carney-Trump Call 'Very Intense and Delicate' as Canada Braces for Midnight 50% Tariff Deadline
events.detail: Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke by phone with President Trump on Monday afternoon ahead of the 50% Section 338 tariffs — covering roughly $20 billion of Canadian dairy, alcohol, and motor-vehicle goods — set to take effect 12:01am EDT Wednesday, August 19. Carney declined to detail the call, describing the negotiations only as 'very intense and delicate' and saying it was 'not the time to negotiate in public.' Canada's Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc and chief negotiator Janice Charette met US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick in Washington the same day — LeBlanc's fourth meeting with Greer in three weeks — saying afterward, 'We're going to continue working. Our job is not yet done.' The main sticking points remain auto-tariff content rules (Canada wants the existing 25% rate cut to 15% based on North American-content eligibility, while the US wants US-content-only credit), unresolved steel and aluminum tariffs, and Canada's dairy supply-management system. Trade experts noted that continued talks hours before the deadline were an encouraging sign, with one former White House trade adviser observing that 'the hardest issues always get resolved at the very last moment.'

events.title: US-Iran MOU Expires Without a Deal — 30-Year Treasury Yield Hits Highest Since 2007, Stocks Slip
events.detail: The 60-day negotiating window under the June 17 US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding expired Monday without a final peace agreement. Trump said the US would not seek an extension, telling Iran to 'put up the white flag of surrender' while adding he felt 'no hurry' and would rely on the naval blockade and upcoming Treasury sanctions to apply pressure; Iran's side blamed unresolved disputes over Strait of Hormuz shipping routes, continued Israeli strikes in Lebanon and Gaza, and an unfunded $300B reconstruction package. The renewed war-risk premium pushed Brent crude up about 2.7% to $90.87/bbl and WTI up 2.6% to $84.50/bbl. Combined with mounting concern over federal debt issuance (national debt nearing $40 trillion) and persistent above-target inflation, the 30-year Treasury yield rose to 5.31-5.32% — its highest level since June 2007 — while the 10-year added to 4.72-4.74%. US equities slipped on the combination of renewed geopolitical risk and higher long-end borrowing costs: the Dow fell 0.5%, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% (snapping a three-week winning streak), and the Nasdaq fell 0.3%.

events.title: China's July Activity Data Misses Across the Board — Industrial Output +4.5%, Retail Sales +0.6%, Investment Slump Deepens

Fixed-asset investment for the first seven months of 2026 contracted 6.7%, deeper than the expected 6.0% decline and worse than H1's -5.7%. Analysts attributed part of the weakness to three typhoons that made landfall in July, disrupting manufacturing hubs in eastern and southern China and forcing millions to evacuate, alongside fading government subsidy support for durable-goods purchases (daily average sales fell to 6.3 billion yuan from 9 billion in June). The data follows Q2 GDP's slowdown to a three-and-a-half-year low of 4.3% and adds pressure on Beijing to deliver stronger fiscal stimulus in the second half to hit its 2026 growth target.

events.title: Canada, US 'Far Apart' in Trade Talks Four Days Before 50% Section 338 Tariffs Hit $20B of Canadian Goods
events.detail: Canadian Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc told a government advisory group Saturday that Canada and the US remain significantly divided in talks meant to head off a fresh round of 50% Section 338 tariffs — covering roughly $20 billion of Canadian autos, alcohol, and dairy exports, including USMCA-qualifying goods — set to take effect at 12:01am EDT Wednesday, August 19. LeBlanc has met US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer four times in three weeks (most recently Thursday, August 13), with talks continuing through the weekend; sticking points include Canada's 25% retaliatory tariff on US vehicles, provincial restrictions on American alcohol sales, and dairy quota arrangements, while Canada is separately pushing for relief from existing US steel and aluminum tariffs. Canadian Chamber of Commerce CEO Candace Laing said both sides are exploring an interim agreement that would bundle the new threat together with tariffs already in place. The standoff is the latest flashpoint in the broader 2026 tariff cycle — alongside the July 24 Section 122/Section 301 transition — that continues to weigh on the US effective tariff rate and cross-border trade volumes.

events.title: July Retail Sales Fall 0.6% — Steepest Drop in Over a Year — as Michigan Sentiment Craters to 51.0; Stocks Slip From Record High
events.detail: The Census Bureau reported July retail and food-services sales fell 0.6% MoM to $763.6 billion, missing the +0.1% forecast and marking the sharpest monthly decline in more than a year (sales remained up 5.0% YoY). The drop was led by motor vehicle and parts dealers (-1.8%), nonstore/online retailers (-2.2%), and gasoline stations (-0.9%), partly offset by gains in clothing (+1.9%) and health/personal care (+0.7%). Separately, the University of Michigan's preliminary August Consumer Sentiment Index tumbled to 51.0 — a 7.6% MoM decline and 12.4% YoY drop, badly missing the 54.5 consensus and down sharply from July's final 55.2 — with year-ahead inflation expectations rising to 4.3% and short-term expectations falling 11%. The weak-demand, weak-sentiment combination pulled US equities off Thursday's record close: the S&P 500 slipped just below flat, the Dow fell about 0.2%, and the Nasdaq-100 dropped about 0.2%, even after Wednesday's flat PPI and Thursday's cooler CPI had briefly driven stocks to fresh highs.

events.title: Day 706 — Sheinbaum Calls Fox a 'Traitor to Democracy' Over Alito Moreno Meeting, Pledges No New Taxes in 2027 Economic Package
events.detail: On September 7, 2026 (Day 706, Monday), back at the National Palace after her ten-state Second Government Report tour, President Sheinbaum sharpened her earlier criticism of the September 4 meeting between former president Vicente Fox and PRI national leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno, mocking it as "the new vision of Mexican politics" and saying it would not go well for them. She called Fox a "traitor to democracy... seen by all Mexicans, first for the desafuero [2004 attempt to bar AMLO from the presidential race] and then for the 2006 electoral fraud," and accused PAN's younger leadership of ties to real-estate corruption scandals, arguing neither PRI nor PAN reaches double digits in support. Separately, ahead of the September 8 delivery of the 2027 Economic Package to Congress, Sheinbaum reiterated "no ha habido un aumento de impuestos ni va a haber" (there has not been a tax increase, nor will there be), saying additional revenue will come from combating tax evasion and shell companies used for false invoicing rather than new levies or new social programs, while keeping austerity in senior government salaries to fund existing welfare spending.

At 10:30 AM she addressed a crowd of more than 10,000 at the Explanada de los Héroes in Monterrey alongside Governor Samuel García, highlighting health, infrastructure, housing and welfare gains in the state and announcing that construction on the Saltillo-Nuevo Laredo passenger rail line — a 396-kilometer project passing through Monterrey, already 3% complete — would receive its formal groundbreaking ("banderazo") in the coming days. At 1:15 PM in Saltillo, Coahuila's Parque Las Maravillas, she detailed a 985-kilometer rail corridor (3% built on the Saltillo-Nuevo Laredo segment), the Saltillo-Monclova highway modernization (158 km, 24% complete), the binational Puerto Verde logistics complex, and a 558-bed regional IMSS hospital under construction (10% complete) alongside new family-medicine units.

No vamos a caer en la provocación." She reported 245,365 Colima residents receive Bienestar welfare programs and, in Jalisco, cited 962,111 beneficiaries of the Pension for Elderly Adults, alongside a confirmation that construction on the Mexico City-Querétaro-Irapuato-León-Guadalajara passenger rail line will begin in 2027. Separately, asked about the previous day's meeting between former president Vicente Fox and PRI national leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno at PRI headquarters, Sheinbaum said the pairing showed they "quieren regresar al pasado de corrupción y privilegios," framing it as an attempted PRI-PAN alliance ahead of the 2027 midterms and contrasting it with her government's welfare programs.

events.detail: On September 4, 2026 (Day 703, Friday), President Sheinbaum held her mañanera from Zacatecas — the first stop of a state-by-state tour following her Second Government Report — alongside Governor David Monreal and her federal Security Cabinet, delivering the findings promised after the August 30 Ojocaliente car bombing. Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said preliminary state-prosecutor analysis found the device used approximately 200 kilograms of explosive material, and confirmed three detentions: Juan Pedro "N" (apprehended August 31 for planting the device), plus Hipólito "N" and Miguel "N" (the latter already wanted on a separate homicide warrant), both linked to a criminal cell operating across Aguascalientes and Zacatecas. Harfuch identified a dispute between CJNG and Cartel del Pacífico cells over routes and territory as one of the main investigative lines, and said the case remains open, with the possibility that additional suspects are operating outside the state. He separately confirmed Mexico holds an active U.S. extradition detention order for Juan Carlos Valencia González ("El Pelón"), the CJNG's new leader following Nemesio "El Mencho" Oseguera's February 2026 death, noting Valencia González holds dual Mexican-American nationality — a detail that lands one day after Sheinbaum's dual-nationality candidacy ban was formally sent to Congress. On the broader security picture, García Harfuch reported 60,000 people arrested for high-impact crimes and 32,000 firearms seized (80% traced to the U.S.) since the administration began, and cited state-level figures showing Zacatecas's daily average of intentional homicides down 96% (from 4.5 in 2021 to 0.2 in 2026) and homicides overall down 85% since September 2024. The visit also included an economic and food-security readout: annual investment up 7.7% in June (public investment +10.9% YoY, private +6%), and record 2026-cycle production of 25.41 million tonnes of maize, 1.36 million tonnes of beans (+300,000 tonnes) and 14.4 billion liters of milk (+900 million liters).

events.title: Day 701 — Sheinbaum Unveils Redesigned Mañanera Stage, Breaking From AMLO-Era Set
events.detail: On September 2, 2026 (Day 701, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum resumed her morning press conference — now used for the "glosa" (line-by-line follow-up) of her Second Government Report — on a newly redesigned stage at the National Palace, the first change to "La Mañanera" set since López Obrador introduced the format in 2018. The old flat burgundy-and-white backdrop was replaced with three panels — two angled outward — forming a semi-curved space, still using burgundy, white and gray tones and retaining the "Conferencia de Prensa" screen. Reporters now sit noticeably closer to the podium than the roughly four-meter distance under the old layout; Sheinbaum remarked, "Ya los veo más cerca, antes casi no los veía." She said the redesign came from her presidential staff rather than any deliberate political signal.

events.title: Day 701 — Sheinbaum Calls Zacatecas Car Bombing "Isolated," Sends Security Cabinet Sept 5
events.detail: On September 2, 2026 (Day 701, Wednesday), asked about the August 30 car bomb attack outside the Ojocaliente, Zacatecas police command, President Sheinbaum called the incident "isolated" while acknowledging it was not the first such attack, and announced her Security Cabinet would travel to Zacatecas on Friday, September 5 to present findings on the criminal group responsible. She separately urged UNAM to consider opening additional undergraduate spaces and faculty positions after the university opened 2,000 new spots, and cited figures from Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde crediting the administration with 27 constitutional reforms and 76 secondary-law reforms since October 2024. Sheinbaum also praised customs and tax authorities for a fuel-theft crackdown, citing the arrest of Fernando Farías Laguna as helping curb contraband and stabilize gasoline prices, and rejected suggestions of a rift with Morena Senate leader Adán Augusto López, saying their direct contact had lessened but coordination with other party leaders continued.

events.title: Day 700 — Sheinbaum Delivers Second Government Report From National Palace, Cites 51% Homicide Drop and Sovereignty Message
events.detail: On September 1, 2026 (Day 700, Tuesday), President Claudia Sheinbaum delivered her Second Government Report ("En Defensa de la Soberanía"-style annual address) from the National Palace at 11:00 AM CDMX time, replacing that day's regular mañanera. Headline claims: intentional homicides down 51% since the administration's October 2024 start (about 44 fewer deaths per day) and high-impact crimes down 32%; the monthly minimum wage risen from 2,800 pesos (2018) to 9,584 pesos, with labor poverty at its lowest level since 2005; annual inflation at 3.12% (July 2026) on a downward trend; the peso trading near 17/USD; roughly 60 million people employed and unemployment at 2.7%; H1 2026 foreign direct investment of approximately $34.97 billion (+2.1% YoY); GDP growth revised to 1.4% QoQ / 1.9% YoY for Q2 2026; and a new welfare push toward 42.86 million beneficiaries by year-end backed by roughly 1 trillion pesos in social spending. On security, the government cited 63,000 people detained for crimes since October 2024, 207 priority targets arrested, 32,824 firearms seized, 519 tonnes of drugs seized and 2,725 clandestine labs dismantled. Health and infrastructure figures included 33 new hospitals, 23+ million "Salud Casa por Casa" home visits, Tren Maya ridership of 2.5 million passengers, and a Pemex financial-debt reduction of roughly $20 billion. Sheinbaum highlighted a new indigenous-rights law and framed welfare programs as "turning love into public policy." She struck a conciliatory, unity-focused tone toward Morena ahead of the 2027 midterms — "que nadie se equivoque: aquí no hay divisiones, aquí no hay rompimientos" — while repeating her sovereignty line that international cooperation "no significa sumisión" and that Mexico's sovereignty "no se negocia, no se entrega y no se comparte." Opposition reaction was sharp: PAN deputy Federico Döring presented a rival "informe real" citing low growth, rising debt, Pemex's financial crisis, insecurity and disappearances; PAN also noted her administration's 0.8% average growth trails AMLO's 1.1%. PRI national leader Alejandro Moreno accused Morena of degrading quality of life and shielding drug traffickers.

events.title: Car Bomb Explodes Outside Police Headquarters in Ojocaliente, Zacatecas — 11 Injured
events.detail: On August 30, 2026 (Sunday) around 7:30 PM local time, an unidentified man parked a vehicle laden with explosives in front of the municipal police (DSPM) command in Ojocaliente, Zacatecas, then fled on foot; the device detonated when an officer approached to inspect it. Eleven people were injured, including civilians and municipal police, at least two seriously. The blast damaged roughly five city blocks — at least seven homes, businesses, private vehicles and patrol units, with windows shattered throughout the area. State Security Secretary Arturo Medina Mayoral said authorities were investigating possible involvement of a Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) cell; the vehicle used had been reported stolen in Jalisco since April, and the explosive materials resembled those used in mining operations. A near-simultaneous explosion in Villa García led to the detention of an 18-year-old who claimed CJNG membership. State officials said the attack was the 17th documented explosive-device attack on security forces in Zacatecas over the prior two years and the 10th of 2026 alone, part of an escalating wave that has included motorcycle-borne devices and improvised metal-pipe bombs ("niples"). State and federal forces reinforced the area following the blast.

events.title: Alcalde Presents Anticorruption Package Modifying 19 Laws, Creating 2 New Ones
events.detail: On August 30, 2026 (Sunday), Presidential Legal Counsel Luisa María Alcalde presented Sheinbaum's anticorruption reform package to Morena's Senate caucus, ahead of formal introduction to Congress. The package modifies 19 existing laws and creates two new ones, introducing real-time technological monitoring of public spending, tighter oversight of government contracting, and mandatory "proactive transparency" in public tenders — publishing bidding information without waiting for citizen requests. The design, led by Anticorruption and Good Government Secretary Raquel Buenrostro with input from the Federal Administrative Justice Tribunal and the Federal Auditor's Office (ASF), also aims to strengthen those two institutions' capacity to pursue corruption and good-governance cases. Separately, Morena's Senate bloc proposed federal deputy Higinio Martínez to preside over the Senate's Mesa Directiva for the third year of the LXVI Legislature.

events.title: Day 697 — Government Launches 14-Spot Media Campaign Ahead of Sept 1 Second Government Report
events.detail: On August 29, 2026 (Day 697, Saturday), the Sheinbaum government began distributing a 14-spot promotional media campaign across television, radio and digital platforms ahead of the September 1 Second Government Report, using the legally permitted pre-report window for official messaging ("hay un periodo en el que el gobierno puede difundir información"). The spots assert the monthly minimum wage rose from 2,800 pesos in 2018 to 9,584 pesos, pushing labor poverty to its lowest level since 2005; highlight construction of 401 preparatory schools, 13 Rosario Castellanos universities and 25 Benito Juárez universities plus rehabilitation of 73,000 school campuses by end of 2026; and tout five economic indicators — rising minimum wage, low unemployment, falling inflation and basic-basket costs, a strong peso, and record foreign direct investment — alongside the absence of any "gasolinazo" fuel-price shock during the administration. A security-themed spot cites a 51% drop in homicides and a National Guard strength of 130,000 active personnel.

events.title: Day 696 — Sheinbaum Says Economy 'Doing Well Despite Tariffs,' Cites 51% Drop in Daily Homicides Ahead of Second Report
events.detail: On August 28, 2026 (Day 696, Friday), four days before her Second Government Report, President Sheinbaum said Mexico's economy is going "muy bien" despite U.S. tariffs having hit automobile exports, pointing to Plan México and the Polos de Desarrollo para el Bienestar investment incentives as buffers, and declared herself "very optimistic" about the economy, security and living standards: "México va mejor, México va bien." On security, the government reported the daily average of homicides has fallen 51% since the start of her administration — from 86.9 per day in September 2024 to 42.5 per day in July 2026. She also proposed restricting cellphone use in classrooms, saying neither students nor teachers should use digital devices during school hours, citing psychomotor-skill development and pointing to other countries reverting to pencil-and-paper methods.

events.title: Day 694 — Sheinbaum Signs Overhaul of 38-Year-Old Environmental Law, Sends It to Congress
events.detail: On August 26, 2026 (Day 694, Wednesday), President Sheinbaum signed an initiative to overhaul the Ley General del Equilibrio Ecológico y la Protección al Ambiente (LGEEPA), Mexico's core environmental statute, unchanged in substance since 1988 (last major update 1995). Environment Secretary Alicia Bárcena presented the ten guiding principles at the mañanera, framing the bill around ecological justice: an earlier and broader Strategic Environmental Assessment requirement for large projects, a ban on splitting projects into smaller pieces to dodge regional review, new restoration programs for rivers, mangroves, coastlines and forests, financial compensation for communities that protect natural areas, and new protections for environmental defenders. The initiative — proposed under the title Ley General de Protección Ecológica y Justicia Ambiental — now goes to the Chamber of Deputies for debate.

events.title: Day 693 — Sinaloa Congress Names Graciela Domínguez Nava Interim Governor, 31-6
events.detail: On August 25, 2026 (Day 693, Tuesday), the Sinaloa Congress voted 31 in favor to 6 against, with zero abstentions, to designate Graciela Domínguez Nava as interim governor, resolving the succession question left open when the legislature approved Rubén Rocha Moya's indefinite leave on August 23. The session had originally been scheduled for Monday, August 24 but was suspended and reconvened the following day. Domínguez Nava, a Morena sociologist and former Sinaloa state deputy (2018–2021) and Secretary of Public Education and Culture (2021–2024) who was also serving as federal deputy for Mazatlán's District 1 before taking leave in June, becomes the state's third governor of 2026 after Rocha Moya and interim predecessor Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde.

events.title: Day 692 — US Reopens Border to Mexican Cattle Exports at Agua Prieta, Sonora After 14-Month Screwworm Ban
events.detail: On August 24, 2026 (Day 692, Monday), the United States reopened the Agua Prieta (Sonora)–Douglas (Arizona) crossing to Mexican cattle exports, ending a suspension imposed after the first New World screwworm (gusano barrenador) case was detected in a Chiapas bovine in November 2024; the ban had blocked roughly 1.7 million head of cattle worth an estimated $2.2 billion. President Sheinbaum said she received a letter from U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins notifying her of the decision. The reopening follows a joint SADER–SENASICA–USDA sanitary action plan and enhanced traceability across a 200-km radius in Sonora and Chihuahua; an initial shipment of roughly 750 head crossed on the first day, with a target of 1,700–2,000 head per day at full capacity. Additional crossings — San Jerónimo-Santa Teresa and Puerto Palomas-Columbus, both linking Chihuahua to New Mexico — are slated to follow in a staggered rollout.

events.title: Day 692 — Sheinbaum Calls PRI's Alito Moreno "Entreguista, Traidor" Over US Tour, Flags $120K Consultancy Contract to INE
events.detail: On August 24, 2026 (Day 692, Monday), President Sheinbaum escalated her criticism of PRI national leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno Cárdenas, calling him "entreguista, traidor" over his repeated trips to Washington to lobby U.S. officials against her government. She said it was up to the INE to determine whether Moreno's reported $120,000-a-month contract with Washington firm Concord Hill Strategies — covering trip logistics and image/wardrobe coaching for his meetings with Trump administration and Congressional officials — violated Mexican political-party financing rules, adding that his "funciones están en EEUU y no en México." The comments follow Interior Undersecretary Ariadna Montiel's earlier accusation that Moreno's US visits sought "protección" from domestic corruption investigations. Separately, Sheinbaum said she was not consulted on Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya's brief Aug 21 return to office — "me enteré por la publicación" — and deferred to the state Congress on the succession.

events.title: Day 691 — Sinaloa Congress Unanimously Approves Rocha Moya's Indefinite Leave
events.detail: On August 23, 2026 (Day 691, Sunday), the Sinaloa state Congress met in an extraordinary session and voted unanimously (all nine deputies present) to approve Rubén Rocha Moya's indefinite leave from the governorship, two days after he briefly returned to the post over a U.S. DOJ indictment tying him to the Sinaloa Cartel's "Los Chapitos" faction. Deputies deferred the question of who becomes interim governor to a Monday, August 24 session at 11:00 a.m., with General Secretary of Government Yeraldine Bonilla Valverde — who had already served as interim governor once, from May to August — administering the state in the meantime and seen as a likely pick to resume the role.

events.title: Day 690 — Rocha Moya Requests Indefinite Leave Again After Sheinbaum, Morena Distance Themselves
events.detail: On August 22, 2026 (Day 690, Saturday) at 6:40 p.m., Rubén Rocha Moya requested leave from the Sinaloa governorship for a second time — an indefinite leave submitted by letter to the state Congress — just one day after unilaterally reincorporating himself into the post over the April 29 U.S. DOJ indictment tying him to the Sinaloa Cartel's "Los Chapitos" faction. President Sheinbaum publicly distanced herself from his return, saying "Sinaloa, la nación y el movimiento de transformación están por encima de todo" and that "ningún interés personal" should be placed above "los intereses del pueblo y de la Nación," warning against "ambición desnuda del poder por el poder"; Morena and the Interior Secretariat also publicly broke with him. Former DEA director Derek Maltz called for Rocha's arrest and deportation. The Sinaloa Congress suspended its session to select an interim governor, postponing the decision.

events.title: Trump Posts Second AI-Generated Image Claiming 'Hundreds of Billions' in Intel Stock Gains
events.detail: President Trump posted an AI-generated image to Truth Social early Monday, September 7, 2026, depicting himself day-trading Intel stock from $20 to $95 a share, captioned with a claim of making 'Hundreds of Billions of Dollars.' It was the second time Trump shared the identical image style — an earlier version last September showed Intel rising from $20 to $30, after the government took a 9.9% stake in the chipmaker. Intel shares closed at $95.80 on September 4 and touched $95.89 two days later, nearly quadrupling off a 52-week low of $24.05, but the largest documented paper gain the government holds on record is roughly $33 billion — far short of Trump's 'hundreds of billions' claim, which he did not substantiate with specific holdings or a time period. Ethics watchdogs have flagged the pattern of Trump publicly touting stocks the government holds a stake in.

events.title: Trump Signs Executive Order on Beef Country-of-Origin Labeling
events.detail: President Trump signed an executive order behind closed doors at the White House on Friday, September 4, 2026, at 1:30 p.m. ET addressing country-of-origin labeling requirements for beef, sources familiar with the matter said. The move follows Trump's efforts to lower record-high beef prices, including an order last month temporarily allowing up to 300,000 metric tons of lower-tariff beef imports to enter the country without the higher 'out-of-quota' rate, aimed at giving the administration time to rebuild the US cattle herd. Agricultural groups have been split: some ranchers back mandatory country-of-origin labeling as a boost to domestic producers and consumer transparency, while groups reliant on imports have opposed the broader tariff-relief push as disadvantaging US producers.

events.title: Foreign-Born Population Falls 2.9 Million Since Trump Took Office, First Sustained Decline Since 1930s
events.detail: A Center for Immigration Studies analysis of Census Bureau household survey data, released Thursday, September 3, 2026, found the total US foreign-born population fell 2.9 million from January 2025 (53.3 million) to July 2026 (50.5 million) — the illegal immigrant population accounting for most of the drop, an estimated 2.3 million decline from 15.8 million to 13.5 million, while the legal immigrant population fell roughly 600,000. CIS research director Steven Camarota called it the first sustained net decrease in US migration since the 1930s, reversing an 8.3 million increase during the post-COVID border surge under the Biden administration. CIS attributed the decline to border enforcement and interior removals; the Current Population Survey underlying the estimate covers about 60,000 households and carries a margin of error of roughly ±1 million.

events.title: Bessent Vows to 'Economically Asphyxiate' Iran, Targets IRGC Offshore Assets
events.detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday, September 1, 2026, at a G20 finance ministerial discussion moderated by Larry Kudlow, 'We are going to economically asphyxiate this regime,' outlining plans to freeze Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps offshore accounts — including trust-company holdings in the British Virgin Islands — and roughly $100 million in luxury real estate held globally. Bessent said the administration would pursue secondary sanctions barring entities that do business with the IRGC, including airline-leasing companies, from the US dollar system, Federal Reserve wire transfers, and SWIFT access, with any recovered proceeds potentially going to terror victims or the Iranian people. The push came alongside the renewed CENTCOM-IRGC exchange of strikes.

events.title: Trump Meets Oil Refiners at White House to Push Down $4-a-Gallon Gas Prices
events.detail: President Trump met Tuesday, September 1, 2026, with executives from small, medium, and large oil refiners and distributors at the White House — alongside Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, Energy Secretary Chris Wright, and National Energy Dominance Council Executive Director Jarrod Agen — to discuss expanding US refining capacity and lowering pump prices, which have held near $4.10/gallon nationally amid the renewed Iran war. Discussion touched on regulatory rollbacks, faster permitting, and additional refinery investment; Exxon was reportedly not among the invited companies. The meeting followed the administration's Venezuela oil deal, under which the US secured majority control of 65 billion barrels of proven reserves.

events.title: US Imposes New 10% Section 301 Tariff on Mexico Over Forced-Labor Import Enforcement Gaps
events.detail: The Office of the US Trade Representative announced the results of a Section 301 forced-labor investigation covering 60 economies, imposing new ad valorem tariffs effective July 24–25, 2026. Mexico was placed in the more favorable 10% tier (rather than the 12.5% tier applied to countries with no forced-labor import prohibition at all) because USTR determined it has import bans on the books but has failed to effectively enforce them against goods transiting its supply chains. Crucially, Mexican goods that qualify for duty-free treatment under USMCA rules of origin remain exempt from the new tariff, so the measure primarily affects the roughly 11-16% of Mexico-US trade that does not claim USMCA preference. The action landed in the middle of the ongoing USMCA joint-review negotiations and added a new friction point alongside earlier tariff threats on autos, steel, aluminum, and copper.

sources.name: Office of the United States Trade Representative

events.title: Trump Threatens 30% Reciprocal Tariff on Mexico Starting August 1
events.detail: President Trump announced that reciprocal tariffs on Mexican goods would rise to 30% effective August 1, 2026, escalating pressure during the ongoing USMCA joint review process. The threat came roughly two weeks after the US declined to renew USMCA on its current 16-year terms at the July 1 joint review, and as bilateral negotiating rounds on automotive rules of origin, steel, and aluminum continued. As of mid-July, USMCA-qualifying goods (an estimated 89% of Mexico-US trade) continued to enter under the existing 0% preferential rate, with the 30% threat aimed at non-qualifying goods and intended as leverage ahead of the next negotiating round scheduled for the week of July 20.

events.title: Banxico Holds Benchmark Rate at 6.5% in Unanimous Vote, Signals End of Easing Cycle
events.detail: The Bank of Mexico's governing board unanimously voted to hold its benchmark interest rate at 6.5% at its June 25, 2026 meeting, confirming the two-year easing cycle that began in March 2024 has concluded. Headline inflation continued to ease, falling from 4.45% in April to 3.55% by mid-June, within Banxico's target tolerance range. Policymakers signaled they will likely keep the rate at this level going forward, citing upside risks from trade disruptions tied to the ongoing USMCA review, geopolitical tensions, persistent core inflation, and possible peso depreciation.

events.title: Banxico Cuts Benchmark Rate to 6.5% in Split Vote, Signals End of Two-Year Easing Cycle
events.detail: Mexico's central bank (Banco de México / Banxico) voted 3-2 to cut its benchmark overnight interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.5% — the lowest level since May 2022 — following April inflation data showing a first deceleration since December 2025. The governing board simultaneously signaled this cut marked the end of a two-year-plus easing cycle that had lowered rates from the August 2023 peak of 11.25%. Board members in the minority voted to hold rates, citing continued uncertainty over US tariff impacts on inflation and peso stability. The peso traded at approximately 17.31 per dollar in early May, representing significant strengthening from the 2025 average of approximately 19.20. The rate decision comes against a complex macroeconomic backdrop: while inflation is moderating and the peso has strengthened, Mexico's economy contracted in Q1 2026 (largest decline in over a year) with investment falling 6.6% in 2025. The Banxico decision was interpreted as a signal that monetary policy has done its work and that structural reforms — fiscal stimulus, investment promotion through Plan México Acciones — must now carry the weight of economic revival. The 6.5% rate still provides meaningful real interest rates above the approximately 4% headline inflation reading, preserving Mexico's financial stability credentials.

events.title: Mexico's Labor Poverty Rate Hits Historic Low at 32.3% in Q4 2025, Despite GDP Contraction Warnings
events.detail: Mexico's Labor Ministry (STPS) and CONEVAL released Q4 2025 labor poverty data on May 6, 2026, confirming a historic milestone: the share of Mexicans in households unable to cover basic food needs with wage income fell to 32.3% — the lowest on record since the measure was introduced. Labor Minister Marath Bolaños highlighted the figure as evidence that the minimum wage increases (cumulative 283% since 2018 under AMLO and Sheinbaum) have translated into genuine material gains for low-income workers. Mexico raised the minimum wage again in January 2026 to MX$278.80/day (approximately $16.10/day), the highest nominal level since the modern wage was established. However, the milestone came amid contradictory signals: the Q1 2026 GDP contraction of 0.8% — confirmed by INEGI on April 30 — created downside risk for formal employment in the near term. Bloomberg's May 6 analysis argued that 'Mexico will lose more from a bad USMCA rewrite than from no deal,' noting that the agreement generates approximately $839 billion in annual bilateral trade and sustains millions of formal jobs in manufacturing, agriculture, and services. The labor poverty reduction is credited to formal job creation driven by nearshoring investment — FDI into Mexico's manufacturing sector hit $36.9 billion in 2024, the highest on record — and the sustained minimum wage policy. Critics noted that 32.3% labor poverty still means nearly one in three Mexicans cannot cover basic food needs through labor income alone.

events.title: Mexico's Sovereign Infrastructure Fund (MIP) Seeks to Deploy $12 Billion; World Cup Airspace Security Decree Published
events.detail: Mexico's sovereign infrastructure fund (Fondo Mexicano del Petróleo para la Estabilización y el Desarrollo, MIP) announced it is actively seeking to deploy USD $12 billion in new infrastructure investments — a major complement to the Plan México Acciones framework unveiled the previous day. The deployment targets strategic infrastructure including ports, rail corridors, industrial parks, and energy grid upgrades to support the nearshoring manufacturing boom. Separately, on May 5, Mexico's Secretariat of National Defense (SEDENA) published a formal decree establishing four Zones of Surveillance and Protection of Mexican Airspace (ZVP) for the FIFA World Cup period running from May 11 through July 20, 2026 — covering Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Monterrey. The decree operationalizes Mexico's counter-drone (CUAS) commitments and coordinates military airspace control with civilian aviation authorities. Mexico City's Benito Juárez Airport simultaneously completed three-day tactical exercises simulating hijacking, hostage-taking, and CBRN (chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear) scenarios. The dual announcements — major investment mobilization and World Cup security finalization — reflected the Sheinbaum government's effort to project institutional capacity despite the Sinaloa governor crisis and US sovereignty disputes of the preceding week.

events.title: Sheinbaum Unveils Plan México Acciones: MX$5.6 Trillion Infrastructure Push to Revive Contracting Economy
events.detail: President Claudia Sheinbaum unveiled 'Plan México Acciones,' an expanded investment framework designed to reverse Mexico's economic contraction after Q1 2026 posted the country's largest GDP decline in over a year. The plan encompasses a MX$5.6 trillion (approximately USD $407 billion) public-private infrastructure investment pipeline for 2026–2030, immediate accelerated tax deductions of 41–91% on new fixed-asset investments, and a unified digital foreign trade platform to reduce bureaucratic friction for exporters. Mexico's sovereign infrastructure fund (MIP) separately announced plans to deploy USD $12 billion in new infrastructure projects. The plan directly responds to a 2025 investment contraction of 6.6% — driven by investor uncertainty over the judicial reform, USMCA tariff tensions, and security concerns. Sheinbaum framed the initiative as Mexico's response to the nearshoring opportunity, with dozens of Asian and US manufacturing companies seeking to relocate supply chains from China to Mexico. The plan attracted cautious interest from the private sector, though business associations noted that judicial certainty and rule-of-law improvements — not tax incentives alone — were the primary investment constraints. Bloomberg noted the initiative came as Mexico sought to project economic confidence ahead of the May 25 USMCA formal review round.

events.title: INEGI Flash Estimate: Mexico's Economy Contracted 0.8% in Q1 2026, All Sectors Declined
events.detail: Mexico's national statistics agency (INEGI) released its flash GDP estimate for Q1 2026 on April 30, showing the economy contracted 0.8% quarter-over-quarter — the worst sequential decline since Q4 2024 and a steeper fall than market consensus. All three major sectors declined: primary activities (agriculture, livestock, fishing) fell 1.4%; industrial activities (manufacturing, construction, mining) fell 1.1%; and tertiary activities (services, commerce, tourism) declined 0.6%. Year-over-year, the economy grew only 0.2% in seasonally adjusted terms, essentially stagnating. The contraction reflected: continued investment uncertainty stemming from the 2024 judicial reform's impact on rule-of-law perceptions; the 25% US tariff on non-USMCA qualifying goods weighing on export-oriented manufacturing; construction delays in major government infrastructure projects; and a deceleration in consumption spending. The data directly prompted Sheinbaum to announce Plan México Acciones four days later (May 4) — a MX$5.6 trillion public-private investment framework intended to reverse the contraction trend. Banxico responded with a 25bp rate cut to 6.5% (May 7). Mexico's full-year 2026 GDP growth forecast was revised down to approximately 1.3%, driven largely by the anticipated World Cup tourism boost in Q2–Q3.

events.title: Sheinbaum Signs Steel Industry Promotion Agreement: All Federal Projects Must Use Mexican Steel
events.detail: President Claudia Sheinbaum signed the 'Acuerdo para el Fomento de la Industria Siderúrgica Nacional' (Agreement for the Promotion of the National Steel Industry) on April 29, 2026, requiring all federal public works projects to use domestically produced steel and iron. The agreement covers 19 federal agencies and three industry chambers — the Cámara Nacional del Acero (Canacero), the Cámara Nacional de la Industria de la Construcción (CNIC), and the Cámara Mexicana de la Industria de la Construcción (CMIC). Anti-Corruption Minister Raquel Buenrostro was designated as the deal's enforcer. Canacero chief Sergio de la Maza called it a 'decisive step' for import substitution, protecting approximately 90,000 direct jobs and providing certainty for over $8 billion in ongoing investment. For 2026, the public sector committed to procuring 150,000 tonnes of reinforcing steel, 150,000 tonnes of structural steel, and over one million tonnes for railway construction. The measure was Sheinbaum's direct economic response after bilateral negotiations to lift US steel and aluminum tariffs failed to reach agreement ahead of the USMCA formal review. By redirecting the government's construction purchasing power — which consumes approximately 60% of Mexico's domestic steel — toward national producers, Mexico essentially launched an import-substitution strategy in the steel sector without a retaliatory tariff. The agreement was unveiled at Wednesday's mañanera alongside the MX$5.6 trillion Plan México Acciones framework announced May 4.
